question: The Commission wants to earmark up to EUR 100 billion for Ukraine in the 2028-2034 budget, while itself admitting that the country’s future needs cannot be predicted. Even so, it is requesting a huge margin for further expenditure in advance. This EUR 100 billion is in addition to the Global Europe instrument, which is already generous in its own right. 1.
Why is the Commission requesting up to EUR 100 billion when it itself admits that it cannot predict Ukraine’s needs?
What is preventing the Commission from proposing a specific amount only once it is able to say what the money will be spent on?
In the Commission’s view, is there a ceiling on support for Ukraine, or should every further bill be paid regardless of the amount?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (25.11.2026) The proposed funding of up to EUR 100 billion for Ukraine under the next Multiannual Financial Framework (MFF) is intended to provide Ukraine with predictable assistance for recovery, reconstruction and modernisation, as well as to safeguard its macro-financial stability, rule of law and path towards EU accession, while facing war time challenges.

Support to Ukraine will continue to be based on appropriate conditionality, regular assessments of Ukraine's progress in implementing reforms, and appropriate monitoring, audit and control mechanisms to safeguard the use of funds and prevent fraud and corruption, as is the case currently under the Ukraine Plan, Pillar I of the Ukraine Facility1.
The precise amounts to be provided annually from the Ukraine Reserve will depend on needs and will be established by the Budgetary Authority in the annual budgetary procedure.

Continued support to Ukraine under the next MFF will make it possible to combine strong and predictable support to Ukraine with the advancement of the EU’s broader external policy objectives; supporting Ukraine is not simply an act of solidarity, it is also a question of European security and stability.
